description: Cancel-invoice cron re-processed every upstream cancel row on every pass and overwrote the recorded outcome with `ignored` — the dedupe compared a microsecond upstream timestamp against `cancel_records.source_ts`, which is written from a JS Date (milliseconds), so the stored row always looked older than its own source
reproSteps: Point a dev backend at a DB with cancel_invoice rows + a running cron → wait 2 passes (~4 min) → the row's outcome flips from `cancelled`/`cancelled_with_putback` to `ignored` ("order … already cancelled") and `last_update_date` keeps moving; the admin list loses the true outcome and the page reloads forever
remarks: Fixed in commit b447a25b — `fetchCancelRows` compares at millisecond precision (`date_trunc('milliseconds', …)`); regression test "µs-precision upstream stamp is not treated as an update on every pass". Outcomes already overwritten in shared/live DBs are log text only — the cancellations/allocations were never re-applied (already-cancelled orders short-circuit); dev DB repaired manually
